entity.name: Edgar Allan Poe
entity.description: The master of macabre who invented detective fiction and died under circumstances as mysterious as his stories. Poe pioneered the short story, wrote The Raven, and married his 13-year-old cousin. He was the first major American author to live by writing alone, and it nearly starved him.

story.name: Edgar Allan Poe
story.description: Orphaned in Boston, expelled from West Point, publishing The Raven in New York to instant fame, and dying delirious in a Baltimore gutter at 40. The tortured arc of America's master of the macabre.

moments.name: Edgar Poe Is Born to Two Traveling Actors in Boston
moments.subtitle: Both parents will be gone within two years, leaving the future master of horror an orphan
moments.description: On 19 January 1809, Edgar Poe was born in Boston, Massachusetts, the second child of actors David Poe Jr. and Elizabeth Arnold Hopkins Poe. His father abandoned the family in 1810, and his mother died of tuberculosis in 1811, leaving two-year-old Edgar effectively orphaned. The boy was taken in by John and Frances Allan, a prosperous merchant family in Richmond, Virginia, who gave him the middle name Allan but never formally adopted him. Poe's fraught relationship with his foster father, marked by disputes over money and gambling debts, would shape his lifelong financial struggles and emotional turbulence.

moments.name: Poe Gets Himself Court-Martialed at West Point on Purpose
moments.subtitle: After his foster father disowns him, the cadet stops attending class to force his own dismissal
moments.description: On 8 February 1831, cadet Edgar Allan Poe was court-martialed at the United States Military Academy at West Point for gross neglect of duty and disobedience of orders. Poe had deliberately stopped attending formations, classes, and church to engineer his expulsion after his foster father John Allan disowned him following Allan's remarriage in October 1830. Poe pleaded not guilty to induce a definitive dismissal rather than a lesser punishment. Before leaving, Poe convinced fellow cadets to fund his third poetry collection, raising about $170 from students who donated up to 75 cents each. They likely expected satirical verse about their officers, not serious poetry.
moments.address: United States Military Academy, West Point, New York

moments.name: Poe Publishes "The Raven" and Becomes Instantly Famous
moments.subtitle: The poem makes the struggling writer a household name but earns him roughly nine dollars
moments.description: In January 1845, Edgar Allan Poe published his narrative poem The Raven in the New York Evening Mirror. The 18-stanza poem about a grief-stricken man visited by a raven that repeats the word Nevermore became an immediate sensation, reprinted across newspapers nationwide and making Poe a celebrity. Despite the poem's enormous popularity, Poe was paid very little for it, reportedly around nine dollars. At age 36, Poe had finally achieved the fame he had long sought, but the financial rewards remained elusive. The Raven remains one of the most widely recognized poems in American literature and cemented Poe's reputation as a master of atmosphere and dread.
moments.address: New York Evening Mirror, New York City

moments.name: A 27-Year-Old Poe Marries His 13-Year-Old Cousin Virginia Clemm
moments.subtitle: The marriage license lists her age as 21, off by eight years
moments.description: On 16 May 1836, 27-year-old Edgar Allan Poe married his first cousin Virginia Clemm in Richmond, Virginia. Virginia was 13 years old, though the marriage license recorded her age as 21. Poe had obtained a marriage bond the previous September in Baltimore when Virginia was still 12. The couple had been living with Virginia's mother, Maria Clemm, since 1831. Despite the age gap, accounts describe the marriage as devoted, with Virginia serving as Poe's muse and emotional anchor. Her slow death from tuberculosis beginning in 1842 devastated Poe and inspired some of his most haunting works. She died on 30 January 1847, and Poe survived her by less than three years.

moments.name: Poe Is Found Delirious in a Baltimore Gutter and Dies Four Days Later
moments.subtitle: Wearing clothes that aren't his own, the author of mystery fiction becomes his own greatest mystery
moments.description: On 3 October 1849, writer Joseph Walker found Edgar Allan Poe semiconscious in a gutter outside Gunner's Hall, a Baltimore tavern being used as a polling place. Poe was wearing ill-fitting clothes that were not his own and could not explain how he got there. He was taken to Washington Medical College, where he drifted in and out of consciousness, reportedly calling out the name Reynolds. Poe died on 7 October 1849 at age 40. The cause of death remains one of literature's great mysteries, with theories ranging from alcoholism to rabies to cooping (being kidnapped and forced to vote repeatedly). Poe was buried at Westminster Hall in Baltimore.
